newsitem.title: ITALY: CanalPlus wants to keep close Mediaset tie.
newsitem.headline: CanalPlus wants to keep close Mediaset tie.

text.p: French group Canal Plus said high demand for its bond convertible into shares in Italian broadcaster Mediaset showed the market appreciated Canal Plus's desire to keep close cooperation with Mediaset.

"The demand for the bond issued was three times higher than the amount offered, showing the appreciation of the market for the strategic significance of our permanence in Mediaset's capital," Canal Plus said. The demand also showed market appreciation "for our desire to maintain, through our presence on the board and among Mediaset shareholders, close collaboration with the television group," it said.
Canal Plus announced the launch on Tuesday of a 2.0 billion French franc equity-linked issue expiring February 28, 2002 and exchangeable into Mediaset shares.
Mediaset subsequently lost nearly four percent on Tuesday and closed down 1.31 percent again on Wednesday at 7,259 lire.

Brokers said the fall was due to investors shifting from Mediaset shares to the bond and selling Mediaset stocks because they viewed the operation as a way in for shareholder Nethold, which is due to merge with Canal Plus, to create an escape from Mediaset.

Canal Plus said the bond operation would only be valid if the merger between itself and Nethold, which is jointly controlled by South African-controlled group Richemont and MCL Multi Choice Ltd, was completed by April.

"We are very satisfied with this financing operation which...has allowed us to refinance our investment in Mediaset for the next five years at very advantageous conditions," it quoted chairman and director general Pierre Lescure as saying.
"The close cooperation between Canal Plus and Mediaset brings great benefits for each, both in operational synergy and in the area of acquiring rights," Lescure said.
Mediaset said in a statement later that Lescure's comments clarified the real meaning of Canal Plus' financial operation.
"This removes all doubt about the strategic valency of relations between Canal Plus and Mediaset," it said.

"The two companies are engaged in turning to account a high profile entrepreneurial and corporate partnership to take every opportunity to develop in television communications sectors," Mediaset said.
